Milk Rolls with Whipped Honey Butter

Served at: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)

Serves 8Prep 30 minCook 20 min

Milk Rolls with Whipped Honey Butter are a traditional treat served during the Feast of the Holy Innocents, also known as Childermas. This festival commemorates the biblical story of the Holy Innocents, and these soft, slightly sweet rolls paired with rich honey butter are a comforting, symbolic food enjoyed at the banquet.

Ingredients

  • 3 1/2 cups (440 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1 packet (2 1/4 tsp) active dry yeast
  • 1 cup (240 ml) warm milk (about 110°F/43°C)
  • 1/4 cup (50 g) granulated sugar
  • 1/4 cup (56 g) unsalted butter, melted
  • 1 large egg
  • 1 tsp salt
  • 1/2 tsp vanilla extract
  • For the whipped honey butter:
  • 1/2 cup (113 g) unsalted butter, softened
  • 1/4 cup (85 g) honey
  • 1/2 tsp vanilla extract
  • Pinch of salt

Method

  1. In a small bowl, dissolve yeast in warm milk and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, combine flour, sugar, and salt.
  3. Add the melted butter, egg, vanilla extract, and the yeast mixture to the dry ingredients.
  4. Mix until a soft dough forms, then knead on a floured surface for about 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
  5. Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover with a clean towel, and let it rise in a warm place for about 1 hour or until doubled in size.
  6. Punch down the dough and divide it into 8 equal pieces. Shape each piece into a smooth ball.
  7. Place the rolls on a greased baking sheet, cover, and let them rise for another 30 minutes.
  8. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
  9. Bake the rolls for 18-20 minutes or until golden brown on top.
  10. While the rolls bake, prepare the whipped honey butter by beating the softened butter until fluffy.
  11. Gradually add honey, vanilla extract, and a pinch of salt, continuing to whip until light and creamy.
  12. Serve the warm milk rolls with a generous spread of whipped honey butter.

Tips

  • For extra softness, brush the rolls with melted butter immediately after baking.
  • You can substitute honey in the dough with maple syrup for a different flavor.
  • Store leftover rolls in an airtight container and reheat gently before serving.
